# External SID playback reference

This directory records the separate **GPL-2.0-or-later verification tool** used
to execute self-authored PSID programs with a C64 CPU and compare SID output.
Neither upstream engine is linked into the BSD/zlib Tetorica browser runtime,
Synth, WASM, Native SDK or their source-copy packages. Downloaded upstream
archives, extracted GPL sources, static libraries and the executable stay under
the ignored `build/sid-reference/` directory. No C64 ROM images are downloaded
or included. The adapter itself, `test/helpers/sid_player_reference.cpp`, is
explicitly GPL-2.0-or-later. The Node build provider is BSD-3-Clause.

## Pinned official sources

| Component | Release / revision | Official archive SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [libsidplayfp](https://github.com/libsidplayfp/libsidplayfp/releases/tag/v3.1.2) | 3.1.2 / `b1e8f1deedf41d343123319237c0d008d72cbea7` | `6d16c20e523ac4d3e385531dafe247a830b59bcb4eb73a557f15cf4e7ae6da84` |
| [libresidfp](https://github.com/libsidplayfp/libresidfp/releases/tag/v1.2.3) | 1.2.3 / `32c8525418a643eaed8dfafa3d7039e250050cfa` | `e9b53a984ca708c3e8d9139eb6aad6141f73ffc22d70a020f7966803f4e2f76d` |

Both licenses are GPL version 2 or later. Exact upstream COPYING files are
retained here. The SHA values match the official GitHub release asset digests;
the build provider checks every cached or newly downloaded archive. It uses
release archives, including upstream's generated PSID driver, rather than the
Git source snapshot that would additionally need the xa65 assembler. No
DSP equations, gain or sampling algorithms are patched. The separate
verification build applies the marked initialization-only patch described below.
Hardware exSID / USB SID support and
upstream unit tests are disabled; no hardware drivers or submodules are needed.

libsidplayfp 3.1.2 contains the upstream out-of-bounds-read fix described in its
release notes. A version pin is not a claim that running arbitrary downloaded
C64 programs has been comprehensively security-audited. Inputs and execution
resources are bounded for this verification subset.

## Rebuild and invocation

On macOS or Linux install a C++17 compiler, `make`, `pkg-config`, `tar` and
`curl`. Node.js runs the provider. Autoconf/Automake and xa65 are not needed
because the pinned release archives already contain their generated files.

```sh
node scripts/prepare_sid_reference.mjs
node scripts/prepare_sid_reference.mjs --offline --check
```

The provider exports `prepareSidReference({workDir, offline, force, check})`
and `SID_REFERENCE_PINS`. It returns `{binary, manifest, manifestPath}`.
The manifest records the adapter/provider input hashes, source pins, build
configuration, compiler version, target platform/architecture, exact initialization
patch receipt and executable hash. `--offline`
may rebuild with cached archives; `--check` only validates an existing build.
`--work-dir=PATH` selects another cache/output directory. `--force` creates a
fresh build without removing existing build evidence. Build sources are kept
with that build so the separately linked executable can be inspected/rebuilt.

```text
sid-player-reference INPUT.psid TRACE.json PCM.f32le DURATION_CYCLES SAMPLE_RATE SUBTUNE [PLAY_EVENT_CHUNK]
```

The adapter produces JSON trace plus mono IEEE float32 little-endian PCM,
normalized from libresidfp's signed int16 output by division by 32768.
It prints a small JSON summary on stdout; errors go to stderr with nonzero
exit status. No padding, gain matching, time stretching or PCM equality claim
is applied. Sample count is the count actually generated by the reference
resampler. `PLAY_EVENT_CHUNK` (default 4096, range 1..4096) groups scheduler
events for chunk-invariance checks; these are not CPU cycles.

Supported execution subset: PSID version 2 with header/data offset 124,
explicit PAL and 6581 flags, one SID at $D400, VBI speed, implicit driver
relocation, effective init/play entry points within program RAM $0800..$CFFF,
and an explicit or embedded load address. Subtune numbering is one-based.
The standard header init address 0 resolves to the effective load address;
play address 0 remains an unsupported IRQ-only program.
RSID, PSID-specific/MUS, NTSC/8580/multiple SID, CIA timing, IRQ-only play,
ROM entry points and explicit relocation are rejected. This deliberately
does not establish compatibility with arbitrary `.sid` game files.

Duration is the absolute number of SID/C64 clock cycles from engine reset,
including power-on settling. Supported range is 100,000..60,000,000 cycles;
sample rate is 8,000..96,000 Hz. File size is at most 65,662 bytes; each SID
read/write trace is limited to 1,000,000 events. The parent Node CLI also
applies a wall-clock timeout and records the source input SHA-256.

## ROMs, timing and comparison limits

The adapter explicitly passes null Kernal/BASIC/chargen ROM pointers.
libsidplayfp's `SystemROMBanks.h` supplies its own minimal GPL Kernal stub and
the PSID driver calls the program's init/play routines through its cycle-based
MOS6510/CIA/VIC environment. The self-authored fixtures use no ROM calls.
Upstream supports broader PSID/RSID/BASIC cases with different ROM conditions;
those cases are outside this tool's subset. ROMless fixture success is not a
claim that every PSID/RSID can run without the original ROMs.

The custom `sidbuilder`/`sidemu` forwards read/write/clock/model/sampling to
libresidfp with the same order as upstream's `reSIDfpEmu`. One host initial
condition is explicit: the adapter starts with volume 0, matching Tetorica's
all-zero initial registers, while upstream requests volume 15. Both
`capture.requestedResetVolume` and `capture.referenceResetVolume` are recorded.
This reset condition is not inserted as a synthetic CPU write; the PSID
driver's actual later $D418 = 15 write remains in the trace. A CPU write callback
at scheduler `getTime(EVENT_CLOCK_PHI2) == T` is recorded at zero-based bus-cycle
start `T`: clock the SID through `[T,T+1)`, then commit the write. Thus the trace
declares `cyclePhase: "phi2"`, `writeTiming: "tick-then-commit"`. Register reads
are also captured; replaying writes alone remains an open-loop comparison
when the original program made decisions from SID readback. It is not a
closed-loop validation of Tetorica's OSC3/ENV3/bus read behavior.

For repeatability `powerOnDelay` is fixed to 0; upstream adds its normal 8000
power-on iterations. The capture includes PCM from those cycles that upstream
normally discards. Its end is capped at `durationCycles`, even if the final
scheduler batch crosses the endpoint. `capture.warmupCycles` and actual
`engineEndCycle` make this explicit. `capture.endCycle` is the SID's exact
clamped endpoint; PCM is never clocked further to fill a resampler tail.

The trace replay clock is Tetorica's existing integer PAL 985,248 Hz.
The reference C64 environment actually uses 985,248.611111... Hz, passed to
the upstream SID sampling API as float 985,248.625 Hz. Both values are recorded
separately under `engine`. The small clock difference is not silently fixed.
Upstream's two-stage RESAMPLE also truncates each sample period to 1/1024 of
its input clock. This slightly changes its effective output rate: at a nominal
48 kHz, it is approximately 48,010.47654 Hz, producing 48,730 frames through
1,000,000 SID cycles. This is not CPU execution past the endpoint. The period
integers and calculated `effectiveSampleRateHz` are reported under `engine`;
all actually generated frames are retained without compensating this behavior.
libresidfp's RESAMPLE sampling, analog filter model and output stage differ
from Tetorica's simplified chips/m6581 core. Measurements describe those
differences; external-reference comparison is not proof of real-hardware
identity, and Native/WASM equality is a separate portability check.

## Verification-only initialization patch

The reference is explicitly identified as **libresidfp
1.2.3+serial-table-init**, not unmodified upstream or real SID hardware.
Unmodified upstream initializes filter lookup tables in parallel. The table
loops call `FilterModelConfig::getNormalizedValue()`, which advances one shared
mutable `Randomnoise.index`. Concurrent unsynchronized updates make those
lookup tables (and consequently reference PCM) vary across fresh processes.
In the initial 4-fixture / 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz investigation, register traces
were identical but PCM differed by up to 43 signed-int16 LSBs between processes.
That observation is not a universal tolerance guarantee.

For reproducible verification, the fresh build copy calls the exact existing
initializers in a fixed serial order: Summer, Mixer, Gain, Resonance, then
VcrVg and VcrIds for 6581; the first four for 8580. The table loops, random
number generator, filter equations, gain and resampler are unchanged. Both
models' initialization is covered because upstream constructs shared filter
configuration objects for both, even though this tool accepts only 6581.
No application/runtime source, calibrated output or pinned original archive
is changed.

[`serial-filter-tables.patch`](serial-filter-tables.patch) is the complete
reviewable diff. [`serial-filter-tables.json`](serial-filter-tables.json)
records each full original/prepared file size and SHA-256, plus the diff hash.
The JSON itself is pinned by SHA-256 in the provider and the adapter metadata.
The recipe verifies both original files before writing either, checks both
prepared file hashes, and rejects unexpected originals or changed receipts.
The build manifest includes all patch inputs so an old unpatched executable
cannot be silently reused. The official release archives remain cached intact.

If distributing this GPL-linked tool, retain the relevant licenses and provide
its matching upstream and adapter source plus build instructions under the GPL.
The normal Tetorica Web/Synth distributions do not include this executable.
